title: Customer Lifetime Value
description:
Compute each customer's **lifetime value**: total amount spent and total number of orders. Return customers with at least 1 order.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`, `city`, `country`

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

Output columns: `name`, `total_orders`, `lifetime_value`. Order by `lifetime_value` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com','Chicago','USA'),(4,'Dan','dan@example.com','Mumbai','India'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,1,DATE '2026-02-10','completed',200.00),(3,1,DATE '2026-03-15','completed',150.00),(4,2,DATE '2026-01-20','completed',300.00),(5,3,DATE '2026-04-05','completed',250.00);
solution_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS lifetime_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC

test_cases.description: Alice (3 orders, 450); Bob (1 order, 300); Carol (1 order, 250); Dan no orders

hints: JOIN customers to orders and GROUP BY customer.
Use COUNT(o.id) for orders and SUM(total_amount) for lifetime value.
explanation: The INNER JOIN excludes Dan (no orders). Grouping by customer and computing COUNT + SUM gives the standard CLV (customer lifetime value) report.
